what: This company engineers thermal management systems: equipment that moves heat away from machinery and buildings. Its products range from data centre cooling systems and commercial heating and ventilation equipment to radiators and cooling modules for vehicles and industrial engines.
customers: Data centre operators and their contractors, commercial building owners, school and institutional buyers of heating equipment, and vehicle and off-highway equipment manufacturers.
money: Data centre cooling, commercial HVAC, heat transfer products and indoor air quality equipment.
Thermal systems for cars, trucks, agricultural and construction machinery and industrial engines.
moat: Thermal systems are engineered into a customer's product or building and must be validated, so suppliers are chosen early and kept. The data centre cooling side benefits from scarce engineering capacity and long lead times for equipment, which lets suppliers select the work they take.
risks: Free cash flow was about negative $9.9M in the trailing period, well below net income of $129.8M, as the company invests in capacity.
The shares trade at roughly 56 times earnings, a high multiple that assumes the data centre growth continues for years.
The vehicle thermal business is tied to automotive and construction equipment production, both cyclical and currently soft.
Data centre cooling is attracting heavy investment from larger competitors such as Vertiv, so today's shortage of capacity may not last.
Eight analysts average a $213.13 target against $134.56, a wide gap implying little consensus.
opportunities: Revenue grew from $2.6B to $3.2B in the latest year shown, driven by data centre cooling demand.
AI computing produces far more heat per rack than earlier servers, which raises spending on cooling equipment per facility.
The business mix is shifting from low-margin vehicle parts toward higher-margin climate equipment, which should lift margins structurally.
Debt of $574.4M against $73.5M of cash is manageable relative to earnings.
watch: Whether the data centre cooling order book keeps growing while cash flow turns positive. The growth is real but currently consumes cash, and a high multiple on a cash-burning business leaves no room for a stumble.
